situation: A brief whose IN scope names five items and whose commits deliver three. Two were promised and never shipped, and nothing outside the brief records that.
expected_guard: the two undelivered items are named individually; the summary does not describe the slice as having shipped its brief
must_not: report only what landed, which reads as completeness
describe the slice as delivering its brief when two items did not ship
aggregate the gap into a count — 'two items outstanding' names nothing a reader can act on
judge whether dropping them was right; that is another command's
infer from the absence that the items were descoped, which is a claim no artifact supports
why_this_fixture_exists: This is the mode's headline value and it was in the slice brief's IN scope and did not ship — the omission was found by review rather than by the suite. A mode built to name what a brief promised and did not deliver, whose own brief promised this fixture and did not deliver it, is the defect demonstrating itself.
